name: Isabel Stuart, Countess of Argyll
bio: Isabel Stuart was the second daughter of Stuart, Lord of Lorn, and married Archibald, first Earl of Argyll, whose title dates from 1457. Sigerson, in Bards of the Gael and Gall (1907), dates her poem to 1459.
“Love Untold” is preserved in the Book of the Dean of Lismore, and Sigerson reads in it a hidden romance. It is given here in his English version.

poems.title: Love Untold
poems.author: Isabel Stuart, Countess of Argyll
poems.collection: Bards of the Gael and Gall (1907)
poems.text:
Woe to one whose wound is love,
Be the reason what may be;
Who can heart from heart remove?
Sad the fate that follows me.

Love I gave my Love unknown,
Never tongue the tale may speak;
Soon, unhealed, it shall be shown
In fading face and thinning cheek.

He, to whom I gave my love
(Ear shall hear not, none shall know),
He has bonds eternal wove
For me, — an hundred fold of woe.
